interpretation_contract: Challenge Threshold tells you how sure you need to be under a named value model. It does not tell you how sure you are.

claims.statement: Under the CT-S1 fixed-path reference model, Challenge Threshold is the break-even required-confidence percentage C / (V + C), where V is immediate correction value and C is modeled future inventory value.
claims.denominator: Not applicable; this is the named model definition.
claims.required_context: State that deltaW is zero by construction in the fixed-path implementation and that the reference convention uses p=0.60 with future use at p times correction value of at least 0.05 expected runs.
claims.prohibited_extension: Do not call the formula uniquely correct, a measure of player belief, or an optimal policy.

claims.statement: The untouched September 11-27 confirmation period supplied 24,880 legal state/inventory candidates. Of those, 22,584 had support in both periods under the frozen common-support hierarchy, or 90.7717%.
claims.required_context: Identify the development window as March 25-September 9 and the confirmation window as September 11-27; September 10 is in neither period.
claims.prohibited_extension: Do not describe unsupported states as validated or impute values to them.

claims.statement: Across 22,584 supported matched rows, the unchanged CT-S1 reference had median absolute drift 0.007628 (0.76 percentage points), 90th-percentile drift 0.026143 (2.61 percentage points), and Spearman rank correlation 0.995354 between development and confirmation.
claims.denominator: All 22,584 finite matched supported reference rows, unweighted.
claims.required_context: Describe this as temporal stability of one frozen named convention, not agreement among alternatives or proof of validity. Note that drift is generally small relative to the convention-driven spread.
claims.prohibited_extension: Do not imply that high rank stability validates player confidence, causal decision quality, or model consensus.

claims.statement: Modeling convention remained the dominant caveat: 21,942 of 22,428 complete supported development rows and 21,929 of 22,428 complete supported confirmation rows had CT Model Spread wider than 0.10, about 98% in each period. Another 156 supported rows per period lacked a complete eight-convention spread.
claims.denominator: Complete supported eight-variant grids within each period.
claims.required_context: Define CT Model Spread as the range across the eight chosen conventions, not a distribution or coverage interval. Display it beside any affected reference value. Suppress the 156 supported rows per period with incomplete spread from point-value tables or label them explicitly as incomplete.
claims.prohibited_extension: Do not present the named reference as assumption-insensitive or merge model spread into a confidence interval.

claims.statement: One of three mechanically selected ordinary representatives met the frozen contrast rule. The CT-S1 reference was 0.668030 at 1-1 and 0.595135 at 1-2 in development, and 0.672804 at 1-1 and 0.600331 at 1-2 in confirmation: a called strike three at 1-2 required about 7.2-7.3 percentage points less confidence under the named model.
claims.denominator: One development-selected ordinary contrast meeting the frozen CTS7 eligibility rule in both periods and all eight core implementations.
claims.required_context: Give the complete situation: offense, original called strike, bottom fifth, home team trailing by at least two, bases empty, no outs, and two units. State that score state is a state key, not win-value leverage under the fixed-path expected-runs objective. Alternatives preserved only the direction, not the 7.2-7.3-point magnitude. Show the two failed ordinary representatives alongside the survivor and state the frozen rule: same direction in both periods and all eight alternatives, with at least 0.05 reference separation in each period.
claims.prohibited_extension: Do not generalize this one contrast into a rule for all two-strike counts or say that a player should challenge.

claims.statement: For the surviving contrast, the confirmation 95% game-clustered sampling intervals were 0.648558-0.696556 at 1-1 and 0.574113-0.626422 at 1-2; the corresponding model-spread ranges were 0.587087-0.756986 and 0.509469-0.694697.
claims.denominator: The two confirmation-period states in the surviving ordinary contrast; 2,000 game-clustered replicates per state.
claims.required_context: Label each sampling interval conditional on the frozen reference definition. Label CT Model Spread separately as implementation disagreement. These are per-state intervals; no paired sampling interval was calculated for the difference.
claims.prohibited_extension: Do not call model spread a confidence interval or claim the sampling interval contains all relevant uncertainty.

claims.statement: Two isolated complete CT-S1 builds reproduced 25 generated files byte-for-byte with zero differences or exclusions, left 447 protected inputs unchanged, and passed 99 focused Article 5 tests.
claims.denominator: All generated files in the frozen CTS3-CTS9 chain and all files in the protected-input inventory.
claims.required_context: Describe this as computational reproducibility, not proof that the modeling convention is uniquely correct.
claims.prohibited_extension: Do not use reproducibility to override sensitivity findings or failed contrasts.

claims.statement: A Pascal ABS Challenge Playbook, an optimal challenge policy, or grades of individual player decisions are not supported by CT-S1.
claims.required_context: The player-confidence layer remains unidentified, deltaW is fixed at zero, model spread is material, and only one ordinary representative contrast survived.
claims.prohibited_extension: Do not create action-colored bands, challenge/preserve commands, player grades, or universal situational rules.

claims.statement: The CT-S1 Model Spread grid contains eight frozen one-factor conventions: reference_fixed_0.60 uses future p=0.60, a 0.05-run future-use cutoff, constrained partially pooled count-aware run expectancy, and extra-inning restoration; fixed_0.50 changes future p to 0.50; fixed_0.70 changes future p to 0.70; cutoff_0.00 changes the future-use cutoff to 0.00 runs; cutoff_0.10 changes it to 0.10 runs; re_pooled_count and re_raw change only the correction-value estimator to the accepted Article 4 pooled-count and raw RE288 estimators; and no_extra_inning_restoration changes only the restoration rule.
claims.denominator: The eight core implementations required for every complete CT Model Spread row.
claims.required_context: Describe the seven alternatives as one-factor-at-a-time sensitivity conventions relative to the reference. Future p is a standardization input for valuing future inventory, not player belief. State that public_tracking and selected_transport are diagnostics outside the eight-convention spread grid.
claims.prohibited_extension: Do not describe the eight conventions as an exhaustive set of defensible models, treat CT Model Spread as a confidence interval, or imply that the named reference is uniquely correct.
